- [IRET.1.4b] **Counted-string storage: recycling freelist
    (Rung γ, x-ref [RTCT.1] / [NRTM.1]).** A counted `String`/
    `Bytes` block is drawn from a **size-classed recycling
    freelist** (classes 8 … 4096 bytes) and returned to it on
    release, so a steady-state assert / retract cycle reuses
    blocks: **zero steady-state allocation**, bounded by the peak
    live count per class. This restores the `realtime`
    steady-state-zero-malloc property. A per-size-class **warmup**
    allocation (and any oversized-string allocation) remains — a
    one-time, bounded event before steady state; it is tolerated,
    not a hard failure (`String`/`Bytes` facts function in RT,
    bounded by the intern contract caps [RTCT.7.1]; go_live does
    not forbid it). Eliminating the warmup entirely (a freelist
    presz before go_live) is an optional further refinement where
    a contract requires a strictly allocation-free pump. The
    freelist changes only the allocation *source*, never the
    refcount semantics ([IRET.1.4]), so reclamation balance is
    identical with or without it.
